chunks: [The obligation of migration:] And migration stands in its original position
Allāh has no need towards him who secretly accepts belief or him who openly does so.
Migration will not apply to any one unless he recognizes the proof (of Allāh) on the earth.
Whoever recognizes her and acknowledges her would be a muhājir (immigrant).
Istid'āf (i.e. freedom from the obligation of immigration) does not apply to him whom the proof (of Allāh) reaches and he hears it and his heart preserves it.

key_terms.الِاسْتِضْعَاف: Exemption from obligation due to weakness or inability, here referring to freedom from the duty of migration.
key_terms.الْحُجَّة: The Proof of God, referring to the Imam or the divine authority on earth.
key_terms.الْهِجْرَة: Migration or emigration, specifically referring to leaving one's place for religious or political necessity.

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the obligation of migration (Hijrah) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this passage establishes that the obligation of Hijrah is intrinsically linked to the presence and recognition of the 'Hujjah' (the Imam or Proof of God), making it a duty of those who are aware of his authority rather than merely a physical relocation. It clarifies that exemption (Istid'af) does not apply to those who have genuinely heard and comprehended the Hujjah, emphasizing that spiritual awareness and acknowledgment of divine authority are the primary criteria for this obligation.
